title: cracking-rosetta algorithm entry
description: One curated algorithm in data/algorithms/. This schema documents the shape for editors and external consumers; tools/validate.pl is what actually gates a PR, because the checks that matter most (does hashcat mode 2811 exist in this hashcat? does dynamic_12 exist in this john?) are cross-references no schema can express.

id.description: Stable identifier. MUST equal the filename stem; it is what external automation keys on, so it never changes once published.

name.description: Human-readable name, as an SME would say it.

aliases.description: Other names this algorithm is known by, for search.

expression.description: hx-style expression, e.g. md5(md5($p).$s). The semantic join key: it is what lets a validator assert two tools' identifiers denote the same construction.

category.description: The human axis this entry sits on. primitive: one hash function over the plaintext. composite: a construction over several. iterated: another entry applied N times. encoding: another entry's digest written differently. application: a product's use of a computation another entry also names. protocol: a challenge-response or wire format. kdf: a deliberately slow derivation.

application.description: The product this row is about, when category is 'application' - Joomla, vBulletin, osCommerce. Data rather than punctuation inside name:.

application_version.description: Version constraint the product places on the row, e.g. '>=3.8.5'.

relations.description: Typed edges to other entries. Many-to-many and symmetric: every edge must be mirrored on the entry it names. This is what lets two entries share an expression honestly - the edge says they are the same computation and the distinction says why both rows exist.

kind.description: same-computation: identical bytes in, identical bytes out. encodes: same digest, different textual encoding. input-encoding: same primitive over a re-encoded plaintext. iterates: this entry is the other applied N times. truncates: this entry is the other, cut short. collides-on-subset: agrees only on a degenerate class of inputs, so a tool may crack one entry's vector without denoting it. duplicate-of: no distinction survives and one of these should go.

entry.description: The id of the other entry.

distinction.description: Why both rows exist despite the relation. 'none' is legal only with kind duplicate-of, which is how a merge is proposed in data rather than in a comment.

status.description: needs-review marks an entry a machine created and a human has not yet confirmed - what the upstream-drift PRs emit.

iterations.description: mdxfind -i value. Part of the identity, not a tuning knob: MD5x02 is john's dynamic_2 and MD5x03 is dynamic_3, so the same type at a different iteration count is a different algorithm.

crack.description: Alec Muffett's Crack, historical reference only. Crack delegates to the host crypt(3) and implements nothing itself; see docs/REFERENCES.md.

vectors.description: Test vectors. A vector is what promotes a mapping to tier 'vector'.

source.description: Where this vector came from: hashcat, mdxfind, john, sheet, or a person.

legacy.description: Identifiers from services that no longer exist. Kept because they make old cracking write-ups readable, not because anything can be verified against them.

tier.description: vector: round-tripped locally by that tool under that exact identifier - the only tier meaning proven. upstream: asserted by a project that verifies by recomputation. asserted: a human said so. absent: the tool does not support this algorithm.
